root_cause: The focus trap in MicroModal includes hidden elements (the retry button inside a hidden div) in the focusable nodes list. When Shift+Tab is pressed from the first focusable element (email), the code attempts to focus the last node in the list (the hidden retry button). Focusing a hidden element fails, so focus remains on the email input, breaking reverse tab navigation.
repair_strategy: Modify getFocusableNodes to filter out elements that are hidden via the [hidden] attribute or have a hidden ancestor. This ensures only visible focusable controls participate in the tab order, allowing Shift+Tab to correctly reach the Cancel button.
expected_accessibility_effect: Keyboard navigation within the modal dialog will correctly cycle through visible controls (Email, Confirm, Cancel) in both directions, satisfying WCAG 2.1.1 (Keyboard) and 2.4.3 (Focus Order).
functional_risks: Filtering by closest('[hidden]') may exclude elements that are intentionally hidden but still focusable (e.g., off-screen via CSS transform). However, the modal's controls are all visible and in the viewport.
verification_requirements: Step 10 (Enter on #confirm) closes modal, shows receipt with correct data.
